records.new_gloss_en: to make a process or organization simpler and more efficient by removing unnecessary steps
records.linguistic_reason: Streamline usually means improving efficiency by reducing complexity, not simply reducing size.

records.new_gloss_en: a length of wire, rope, or other material wound into a series of circles
records.linguistic_reason: Coil also operates as a verb and denotes a spiral rather than necessarily an electrical coil.

records.new_gloss_en: a model of a person used for testing, display, or training
records.linguistic_reason: Dummy also means unintelligent person (insult) and an adjective for imitation objects.

records.new_gloss_en: a group of things growing or gathered close together
records.linguistic_reason: Clump denotes a close cluster; verb meaning walk heavily is separate.

records.new_gloss_en: a large natural hole or hollow space in a hillside or underground
records.linguistic_reason: Cave is a natural hollow; the verb 'cave in' means collapse or yield.

records.new_gloss_en: the process of finding and hiring or enlisting people for jobs or membership
records.linguistic_reason: Recruitment covers hiring employees and enrolling volunteers or members.

records.new_gloss_en: a piece of clothing that covers the hand and has separate sections for the fingers
records.linguistic_reason: Glove differs from mitten by the individual finger sections.

records.new_gloss_en: a break or crack in a bone or other hard material
records.linguistic_reason: Fracture refers to both anatomical and material breaks; noun vs verb needs checking.

records.new_gloss_en: the ability of a plan or organism to work successfully or continue existing
records.linguistic_reason: Project feasibility and biological ability to survive are distinct viability senses.

records.new_gloss_en: having similar qualities or characteristics to something else
records.linguistic_reason: Akin generally takes to, and is not identical to kinship noun kin.

records.new_gloss_en: to signal or announce that something important is coming
records.linguistic_reason: Herald also means messenger or announcer as a noun, unlike source verb reading.

records.new_gloss_en: to have or give off a strong unpleasant smell
records.linguistic_reason: Stink can be a noun too; verbal reading matches the source.

records.new_gloss_en: a shape or length that curves round and joins itself, or a repeated sequence of actions
records.linguistic_reason: Physical loop, programming loop and feedback loop have distinct usage frames.

records.new_gloss_en: in a way that requires immediate attention or action
records.linguistic_reason: Urgently emphasizes need for prompt response rather than high speed alone.

records.new_gloss_en: a strong feeling of support and faithfulness toward a person or group
records.linguistic_reason: Loyalty entails continuing allegiance, not uncritical agreement.

records.new_gloss_en: the ability to recover or adapt after difficulties, changes, or stress
records.linguistic_reason: Resilience also denotes the elasticity of physical materials, a technical sense.

records.new_gloss_en: a metal or other joint that allows a door or lid to swing open and closed
records.linguistic_reason: Mechanical hinge attaches turning parts; verb hinge on means depend on.

records.new_gloss_en: a boy or young man, especially in informal British English
records.linguistic_reason: Lad is informal, culturally marked, and generally refers to a male.

records.new_gloss_en: to arrange to receive a publication or service regularly, usually for payment
records.linguistic_reason: Source also contains share subscription and agreement with an opinion, different verb senses.

records.new_gloss_en: to spread into or occupy a place in excessive numbers
records.linguistic_reason: Overrun can instead mean exceed time/budget or invade; its meanings should be separated.

records.new_gloss_en: a continuous low, deep sound such as distant thunder or heavy machinery
records.linguistic_reason: Rumble also serves as a verb and may mean a fight or discovery of a secret.

records.new_gloss_en: to add nutrients or fertilizer to soil or plants to help them grow
records.linguistic_reason: Fertilize also describes causing an egg to develop through fertilization.

records.new_gloss_en: small cubes with numbered or marked faces, used in games of chance
records.linguistic_reason: Dice is typically plural of die; also a verb meaning cut food into small cubes.

records.new_gloss_en: a container with a handle, often used to carry water or other materials
records.linguistic_reason: Bucket denotes a handled container, rather than every kind of vessel.

records.new_gloss_en: measured or extending along the length of something, or over time
records.linguistic_reason: Longitudinal also means relating to longitude in geography, distinct from longitudinal study.

records.new_gloss_en: a message formerly sent using a telegraph system
records.linguistic_reason: Telegrams used encoded transmission over telegraph networks, not ordinary email.

records.new_gloss_en: a place where an event, meeting, or performance takes place
records.linguistic_reason: Venue refers to location of an event; legal venue is a specialized use.

records.new_gloss_en: relating to a relationship in which one event produces or influences another
records.new_gloss_zh: 因果的；原因与结果相关的
records.linguistic_reason: Causal concerns cause and effect rather than mere correlation.

records.new_gloss_en: an item wrapped or packed for delivery
records.linguistic_reason: Parcel also denotes a plot of land and the verb to divide into portions.

records.new_gloss_en: especially noticeable, important, or prominent
records.linguistic_reason: Salient describes a feature that stands out in relevance or perception.

records.new_gloss_en: a device that produces a concentrated beam of light with tightly controlled properties
records.linguistic_reason: Laser refers to the apparatus or the beam called laser light; source combines both.

records.new_gloss_en: the quality of reasoning or acting according to logic and sound judgment
records.linguistic_reason: Rationality concerns reason-guided decisions, not absence of emotion.

records.new_gloss_en: fine, hard, usually white ceramic material used for dishes and cups
records.linguistic_reason: Lowercase china denotes porcelain/tableware; capitalized China is the country.

records.new_gloss_en: a physical, mental, sensory, or developmental impairment, especially in relation to barriers affecting participation
records.linguistic_reason: Disability as impairment, legal status, and interaction with social barriers require respectful context; not equivalent to any temporary difficulty.

records.new_gloss_en: in a calm way that accepts delays or difficulty without becoming annoyed
records.linguistic_reason: Patiently describes tolerance over time rather than passive inaction.

records.new_gloss_en: intensive publicity or exaggerated claims used to generate excitement
records.linguistic_reason: Hype also functions as a verb, and not all publicity is exaggerated.

records.new_gloss_en: property or other assets pledged as security for a loan
records.linguistic_reason: Collateral can be an adjective for secondary or related matters, a different sense.

records.new_gloss_en: a shop or department where medicines are prepared or sold
records.linguistic_reason: Pharmacy denotes dispensing site or profession in other contexts.

records.new_gloss_en: a speech sound produced with substantial obstruction of airflow in the vocal tract
records.linguistic_reason: A consonant may refer to a speech sound or a letter representing one; sound definition is primary.

records.new_gloss_en: showing compassion and a desire to avoid causing suffering
records.linguistic_reason: Humane describes treatment considerate of living beings, distinct from merely human.

records.new_gloss_en: a group of people sharing an experience or characteristic during a defined period
records.linguistic_reason: Cohort often denotes people grouped by an event/time, e.g. birth or study enrollment.

records.new_gloss_en: an instrument with a magnetic needle that indicates direction
records.linguistic_reason: Navigation instrument, not the drawing tool for circles (compasses).

records.new_gloss_en: height above a given level, especially sea level
records.linguistic_reason: Elevation also denotes the act of raising or promotion to a higher status.

records.new_gloss_en: to stick firmly to a surface or another substance
records.linguistic_reason: Adhere to rules/principles is distinct from physical adhesion.

records.new_gloss_en: a person who owns a house, apartment, or land and rents it to someone else
records.linguistic_reason: Landlord is lessor, not tenant; can also mean pub proprietor in British usage.

records.new_gloss_en: strong alcoholic drinks made by distillation, rather than ordinary beer or wine
records.linguistic_reason: North American liquor often means distilled spirits; regional broader uses exist.

records.new_gloss_en: to make an activity or practice illegal
records.linguistic_reason: Outlaw is also a noun for a person outside the law.

records.new_gloss_en: a tax charged on goods brought into or sent out of a country
records.linguistic_reason: Tariff also refers to a list of charges for utilities or services.

records.new_gloss_en: not containing all the necessary parts or information
records.linguistic_reason: Incomplete concerns missing elements rather than necessarily incorrect existing information.

records.new_gloss_en: to raise the hand to the forehead or perform another formal gesture of respect
records.linguistic_reason: Salute as a verb differs from a noun denoting the gesture or words of greeting.
